items: Share your own widgets: Widgets → Get more widgets → Share a widget checks your widget, lists every command it can send, and opens GitHub with the submission filled in. Accepted widgets appear in Browse library for everyone.

The Servers page is now called Multi Server, and shows up to six servers side by side, all the same size and filling the window. It lists who is online on each, and you can add a server or choose which six to show from the page.
The welcome screen on first launch lets you add several servers in a row and shows what the Multi Server page looks like.
A roomier Widgets page: All widgets in the sidebar opens every widget as a tile, grouped and searchable. The sidebar now lists just your favourites, so it no longer needs scrolling.
Tighter spacing in the sidebar, so more fits on smaller screens.
Saved console and player files now go to Documents\Bunker\Exports instead of cluttering Documents.
Export the console to a text file (Save in the Console header), and the Player database to a CSV file that opens in Excel (Export CSV).
A note like this one now appears after Bunker updates. You can open it again any time from Settings → About.
The Ban Manager shows your bans as a sortable table, with the date each ban ends. Click a row to fill in the Steam ID, then press Unban.
A new Servers page shows every saved server at a glance, with one-click Open and a box to say something or run a command on all online servers.
Uninstalling now removes everything, including your saved data (it asks first).
Clicking the X in the corner asks whether to minimise or close. Tick Remember my choice to stop being asked; change it in Settings → General.
Bunker reconnects by itself if the connection to your server drops.
A Bunker icon in the system tray, and Windows notifications for chat watch-words and a lost connection while Bunker is not in front.
Right-click any player in the Player database for the same menu as the Players page, even if they have left.
If you type ordinary words into the console box, Bunker asks whether you meant to say them in chat.
A Command / Chat switch in the console box, so you can talk to players from the console.
Star your favourite widgets to list them first, and choose the colour of chat tags such as [ADMIN].
A cleaner widget page that uses the whole window, and Settings → Updates now lists newer versions of your widgets.
Hide console messages by plugin name (for example [Economics]) or by words.
Update checks no longer run into GitHub's rate limit.
Chat as yourself: set a name, Steam ID and colour in Settings → Chat (needs the small BunkerChat plugin on your server).
Fixed an error when opening the Chat monitor.
Chat looks like it does in the game, with coloured names and [TEAM] tags.
Carbon and Oxide plugin lists appear as a sortable table.
